raw_response:
I'm 69 years old now. I've been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years — my father taught me, and I learned the rest by watching my own fields and talking to my neighbors. I only finished primary school, so I don't read books about farming. I know what works because I've done it, and because Old Wang and the others in my village tell me what they see.

This year I'm keeping my cabbage-chili-cabbage rotation on about 3 mu, and I've got cucumber, eggplant, and kidney beans on the rest. My son works in the county town factory, so it's mostly me and my wife in the fields. We can't hire much labor — 130 to 150 yuan a day is too much for us, we only hire someone when we're really stuck.

For the spring cabbage, I start seedlings in late March in my small cold frame. I transplant in early April. I put down base fertilizer before planting — about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, plus some urea. I topdress once more when the heads start getting big. Cabbage always gets caterpillars, so I spray insecticide a few times. I'll irrigate 5 or 6 times if it's dry. Should be ready by late May.

Right after I cut the spring cabbage in early June, I don't rest — I till quick with my small rotary tiller and put in chili peppers. I start the chili seedlings in April so they're ready. Chili likes the heat, and June is warm enough. I give it base fertilizer at planting and topdress when it flowers. That 1.5 mu of chili can bring good money if the price holds.

Then in August, after the chili slows down, I plant fall cabbage on that same land. It grows until November. Three crops from the same land — that's how we survive on 5 mu.

Cucumber is on 1 mu. I plant in early April with plastic film to keep the soil warm. Cucumber drinks a lot of water — maybe 8 to 10 irrigations. But the electricity for pumping costs money, so if it rains enough I skip. I buy hybrid cucumber seeds, they're expensive but the yield is better.

Eggplant is 1 mu, planted in May. I buy seedlings from the market now — at my age it's easier than raising my own. Just water and fertilize when it starts fruiting.

Kidney beans, half a mu near the house. My wife looks after those. Easy crop, doesn't need much fuss.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, so I'm trying not to waste any. But I won't cut too much — I remember the drought year of 2013, when I tried to save money on fertilizer and the yield dropped badly. A bad year hurts more than saving a few yuan. I use compound fertilizer and urea, that's what I know.

Total costs this year — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, pumping electricity, maybe a few days hired labor — I figure about 4,000 yuan. That's a lot for us. Vegetables sell for more than grain, but you never know the market price until harvest. Last year cucumber was cheap. I just hope this year is average.

For labor, me and my wife do almost everything. Family labor is probably 60 days or so spread across the year. We might hire someone for a day or two during transplanting when we really need extra hands.

If the weather is normal, I expect spring cabbage around 2,000 jin per mu, chili maybe 1,500 to 2,000 jin, fall cabbage about the same, cucumber 2,000 to 2,500 jin, eggplant 1,500 to 2,000 jin, and kidney beans around 1,000 jin. But you never know. I'm hoping for a decent year.
